narrativeReportMd:
# Immunization R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The R6 ballot keeps the same `Immunization` canonical identity, but the local content model is substantially remodeled: several R4 elements are removed or renamed, multiple fields move to `CodeableReference`, and two new error-level invariants can invalidate previously valid R4 instances.

## Scope
This assessment uses the local R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4 core package StructureDefinitions, package metadata, indexes, and locally present terminology files. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are excluded except where an Immunization field locally changes type.

## Main migration themes
The biggest migration theme is representation change rather than cardinality tightening: `reasonCode`/`reasonReference`, `reportOrigin`, `reaction.detail`, `manufacturer`, and protocol dose fields all require JSON-path and generated-model changes. A second theme is data loss risk: `recorded` and `education` disappear without direct local replacements. A third theme is R6-to-R4 loss: new optional R6 fields and widened targets cannot be carried by base R4 without extensions or external resources.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact issues include the `reason` CodeableReference merge, `programEligibility` backbone remodel, protocol dose-number remodel, `manufacturer` type change, `reportOrigin` to `informationSource`, and the new `statusReason` invariant.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for `statusReason` because R6 text and invariant appear inconsistent, for `recorded` and `education` because replacements are not explicit, for funding-program eligibility because R4 lacks the new required program value, and for protocol dose concepts because clinical forecasting can be affected.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some breaks were likely motivated by cleaner R6 modeling patterns, especially `CodeableReference`. Several could have been staged more compatibly by adding optional elements or choice types before removing old names. Optional additions are forward-compatible but still require an R6-to-R4 policy.

## Follow-up analysis
Terminology expansions, official migration notes, and local profile/search-parameter analysis would improve confidence, especially for example ValueSet changes and operational behavior outside the base StructureDefinition.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 Immunization has material breaking changes despite stable canonical identity. Top concerns are CodeableReference remodels, removal of `recorded`/`education`, and new invariants on `statusReason` and `subpotentReason`. Main uncertainty is terminology and official rationale because expansions and narrative change notes were not available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a real transform, not a package-version swap. Update parsers and generated models for renamed/reshaped fields; define policy for removed fields (`recorded`, `education`); add validation prechecks for new invariants; and design R6-to-R4 extension or loss-reporting rules for R6-only fields and widened targets.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas because both local core StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for terminology impact and design rationale because full terminology expansions, official diffs, narrative pages, and ConceptMaps were not available. Base-artifact changes were intentionally excluded by scope.

findings.title: statusReason is now constrained to status = not-done

oldState.summary: R4 allowed statusReason whenever the optional element was populated; no local invariant tied it to status.
oldState.narrativeMd: `Immunization.statusReason` was optional in R4 and described as generally used for `not-done`, but the StructureDefinition did not enforce that condition.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same element but adds root invariant imm-1: statusReason exists only when status is 'not-done'.

constraints.human: statusReason SHALL only be present if the immunization status is 'not-done'

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes the previously advisory relationship into an error-level invariant. The R6 definition/comment also says statusReason may be used for `entered-in-error`, which conflicts with the invariant and needs review.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. An R4 instance with `statusReason` and any status other than `not-done` can be valid in R4 but fail R6 validation with an error-level invariant. Runtime risk is high for validators, import pipelines, and business rules that preserved reasons for `entered-in-error` or other statuses.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Rejecting or dropping status reasons can affect auditability of not-administered or erroneous immunization records.

justification.inferredGoal: Make statusReason usage consistent with not-done immunization events.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `statusReason` valid in the base resource for existing statuses and express the `not-done` preference through warning-level guidance or profiles.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of making `statusReason` usage more consistent is reasonable, but the error-level invariant invalidates R4 records that were structurally valid and the R6 text still mentions `entered-in-error`. With that ambiguity, the level of breakage is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the R4 permissive element and added clearer definition text, a best-practice warning, or a profile-specific invariant for systems that require `status = 'not-done'`. That would preserve old instances while still steering new implementations toward the intended usage.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves historical reasons but weakens uniform base enforcement of the preferred status relationship.

evidence.detail: R4 statusReason has no local invariant restricting the allowed status.
R6 adds an error invariant tying statusReason to status = 'not-done'.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative: it includes the relevant required R4 fields plus a statusReason on `entered-in-error`, which R6 imm-1 rejects.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 turns `statusReason` usage into a hard local constraint. Existing R4 data that carried a reason for statuses other than `not-done` must be changed, dropped, or represented elsewhere before R6 validation. The sharp edge is that the R6 definition text still mentions `entered-in-error`, so implementers should not assume the transform is purely mechanical without checking ballot intent.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: old-valid instances can become new-invalid when `statusReason` is present and `status` is not `not-done`. R6-to-R4 is not a representability problem because R4 is less restrictive. Strict validators and generated invariant checks will surface this as an error, not just a warning.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before validating as R6, scan for `statusReason` where `status != 'not-done'`. Decide whether to change status, move the reason to an extension/audit note, or reject the record for manual review. Include `entered-in-error` test cases because the R6 text and invariant appear inconsistent.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The goal could likely have been achieved less disruptively with guidance text or a warning invariant. Making the invariant an error gives stronger data uniformity but breaks historical records that used the optional element in broader ways.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended because R6's `statusReason` definition says it is used for `not-done` or `entered-in-error`, while imm-1 permits only `not-done`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 turns the formerly advisory relationship between `statusReason` and `status` into an error-level rule. That can reject R4 records that kept a reason for `entered-in-error` or another non-`not-done` status, and the R6 element prose still says the field is used for `not-done` or `entered-in-error`. The computable invariant and the narrative guidance therefore do not line up, so this looks like a standards/design issue rather than a routine migration cleanup.
keyEvidence: R4 `Immunization.statusReason` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with no local invariant tying it to status.
R6 root constraint `imm-1` is error severity: `statusReason.exists() implies status = 'not-done'`.
R6 `statusReason` definition/comment says the reason can apply when the event was not performed or entered in error.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3/trial-use means mature trial-use stability: not normative, but a hard validator break on public-health record content needs clear justification and does not get low-FMM leniency.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `statusReason` and `status` other than `not-done` can fail R6 validation under an error invariant.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes: the base could allow the `entered-in-error` case described in the prose, or make the `not-done` relationship warning-level/profile-specific. The tradeoff is weaker uniform base enforcement.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identified a hard break and a less-breaking alternative; the fresh review puts extra weight on the R6 prose/invariant inconsistency.

findings.title: subpotentReason now requires isSubpotent = true

oldState.summary: R4 allowed subpotentReason independently of the optional isSubpotent flag.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 gave `isSubpotent` a meaningWhenMissing of potent by default, but it did not forbid `subpotentReason` when the flag was absent or false.

newState.summary: R6 adds error invariant imm-2 requiring isSubpotent to exist and be true whenever subpotentReason exists.

constraints.human: subpotentReason SHALL only be present if isSubpotent is 'true'

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes the reason element conditional. It also moves the example ValueSet canonical to `terminology.hl7.org`, but the hard break is the invariant.

facts.newValue: imm-2: subpotentReason.exists() implies (isSubpotent.exists() and isSubpotent = true)

facts.note: Example binding canonical moved; no required-code validation impact by itself.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 record with `subpotentReason` but no `isSubpotent=true` is now invalid. The data pattern is probably less common than core administration fields, but it is a hard validator failure when present.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Subpotency affects clinical interpretation of protection; automated correction should avoid changing clinical meaning without evidence.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure a subpotency reason is only supplied when the dose is explicitly marked subpotent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a warning or a looser invariant that tolerates missing `isSubpotent` when `subpotentReason` exists.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is clinically coherent: a subpotency reason should imply that the dose was subpotent. A less strict rule would reduce migration failures, but it would also preserve the R4 ambiguity where a reason can appear while the boolean is absent or false.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A warning-level rule, or an invariant that rejects only explicit `isSubpotent=false`, would preserve more R4 data. That alternative is incomplete because an absent flag had a potent-by-default meaning in R4, so accepting absent-plus-reason records can still be clinically misleading.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: More tolerant validation preserves old records but leaves clinically ambiguous subpotency assertions in the base resource.

evidence.detail: R4 subpotentReason has no local condition tying it to isSubpotent.
R6 adds an error invariant requiring isSubpotent to be present and true.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows a common mechanical remediation, but setting `isSubpotent` should be confirmed as acceptable for the source data.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a local consistency rule between `subpotentReason` and `isSubpotent`. This is clinically sensible but breaks R4 data that carried a reason without explicitly carrying the boolean flag. The validator effect is an error-level failure at the resource root.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: an old instance can become invalid if it has `subpotentReason` and omits `isSubpotent` or sets it false. R6-to-R4: R4 can still carry both elements, so down-conversion is not a structural problem.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Detect all records with `subpotentReason`. If local rules allow, set `isSubpotent=true`; otherwise route the record for review. Test absent, false, and true flag cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The invariant's intent is probably justified, but a warning-level constraint would have avoided rejecting historical records. The strict form trades migration tolerance for stronger clinical consistency.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 rejects `subpotentReason` unless `isSubpotent` is explicitly true. This is a real old-valid/new-invalid pattern, especially for R4 data that omitted the boolean, but the affected semantics are narrow and clinically coherent: both R4 and R6 say a missing `isSubpotent` means the dose should be considered potent. Requiring an explicit true flag when a subpotency reason is present is proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 `Immunization.subpotentReason` is 0..* CodeableConcept with no local condition.
R4 and R6 `Immunization.isSubpotent` both say missing means the dose is considered potent.
R6 root constraint `imm-2` is error severity: `subpotentReason.exists() implies (isSubpotent.exists() and isSubpotent = true)`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3/trial-use raises some compatibility expectation, but the path-level safety rationale for eliminating an internally inconsistent subpotency assertion is strong enough.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 records with `subpotentReason` and missing or false `isSubpotent` become invalid under R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial: R6 could have used a warning or only rejected explicit `isSubpotent=false`. That would preserve more old records but would continue allowing reason-plus-missing cases even though missing means potent.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's medium impact and partial alternative match the fresh assessment.

findings.title: reasonCode and reasonReference were replaced by reason CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 had two separate repeating elements: reasonCode CodeableConcept and reasonReference Reference(Condition | Observation | DiagnosticReport).
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 separated coded reasons from resource references using different JSON property names.

newState.summary: R6 has one repeating reason element of type CodeableReference targeting Condition, Observation, or DiagnosticReport.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `reason[].concept` for coded/text reasons and `reason[].reference` for justifying resources.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 definition explicitly combines coded/text reasons and references that justify the immunization; it covers the definitions of both R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON properties `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` are not valid R6 Immunization elements. Generated model APIs also change from two collections to one `CodeableReference` collection. Down-conversion is usually possible by splitting concept and reference, but if an R6 CodeableReference carries both in one repetition, R4 loses that pairing.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reasons can represent indications, occupational risks, or clinical conditions; losing them or their pairing can affect analytics and clinical decision support.

justification.inferredGoal: Adopt the R6 CodeableReference pattern for fields that can be either a concept or a resource reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason` CodeableReference for new R6 use.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The CodeableReference merge is consistent with the R6 modeling direction and supports concept/reference pairing. The break is substantial, but a fully compatible transition would leave parallel reason representations that implementations may populate inconsistently.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated elements and added `reason` as the preferred representation. That would preserve R4 JSON, but systems would need rules for precedence, duplication, and whether deprecated reason fields ever disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but creates duplicate same-resource representations and reconciliation rules for the same clinical reason.

evidence.detail: R4 reasonCode is a repeating CodeableConcept with example binding to immunization-reason.
R4 reasonReference is a repeating Reference to Condition, Observation, or DiagnosticReport.
R6 reason is a repeating CodeableReference with the same reference targets and an example reason binding.

examples.examplesMd: R6 can place a concept and a reference in the same CodeableReference repetition; R4 can split the values but cannot preserve that exact association without an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: The reason model is locally remodeled rather than merely renamed. R4 senders used two explicit arrays; R6 senders use one CodeableReference array. This affects validation, JSON paths, FHIRPath expressions, generated model fields, and transforms.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: instances containing `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` become invalid until transformed to `reason[].concept` or `reason[].reference`. R6-to-R4: concept-only and reference-only repetitions can be split, but mixed concept/reference repetitions lose grouping in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `reasonCode` to a separate R6 `reason.concept`; map each R4 `reasonReference` to `reason.reference`. For R6-to-R4, split CodeableReferences and use an extension or manual review if preserving concept-reference pairing matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The CodeableReference pattern is coherent, but the old element names could have been retained temporarily as deprecated fields or compatibility extensions. That would reduce breakage at the cost of duplicative semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4's two reason arrays are replaced by one R6 `CodeableReference` array. R4 JSON paths and generated APIs must change, and reverse conversion can lose a concept/reference pairing when both are present in one R6 repetition. Still, the model consolidation is a coherent R6 pattern and a compatibility-preserving alias approach would create duplicate representations for the same clinical reason.
keyEvidence: R4 has `reasonCode` 0..* CodeableConcept and `reasonReference` 0..* Reference(Condition|Observation|DiagnosticReport).
R6 has `reason` 0..* CodeableReference with the same reference targets and the reason ValueSet on the concept side.
CodeableReference can carry concept and reference in the same repetition, a pairing R4 cannot preserve directly.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3/trial-use means reason migration matters, but this is a mature trial-use area where a well-motivated modeling cleanup can still be acceptable.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` properties are not R6 elements; generated clients also move from two collections to one CodeableReference collection.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial: R6 could have kept deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason`. That preserves old wire format but creates duplicate same-resource semantics and conflict rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treated this as a real but probably justified CodeableReference remodel.

findings.title: reportOrigin was replaced by informationSource CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 reportOrigin was an optional CodeableConcept describing the source of secondarily reported data.

semanticText.definition: The source of the data when the report of the immunization event is not based on information from the person who administered the vaccine.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could record a coded origin such as provider, record, recall, or school, but not a direct source-person/source-organization reference in this element.

newState.summary: R6 informationSource is an optional CodeableReference bound to the same origin ValueSet and can reference Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, or Organization.

semanticText.definition: Typically the source of the data when the report of the immunization event is not based on information from the person who administered the vaccine.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the source-origin semantics but changes both the property name and the datatype representation.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 binding name remains ImmunizationReportOrigin, the binding ValueSet remains immunization-origin, and the definition is a close successor to R4 reportOrigin.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `reportOrigin` uses a property name removed from R6. R6 `informationSource.reference` values have no equivalent R4 field, making down-conversion lossy unless represented through extensions or notes.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Source provenance affects trust in immunization records, especially registry imports and patient-reported histories.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent information source as either a coded origin or a concrete source actor.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `reportOrigin` for coded origin and add an optional source-actor reference for the richer R6 use case.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of representing a concrete information source is reasonable, but replacing and renaming the existing coded-origin field was not necessary to meet it. A less-breaking additive design could have preserved nearly all R4 instances with moderate long-term cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could keep `reportOrigin` as the coded origin and add a separate optional `informationSource` reference, or similar actor field, for Patient, Practitioner, RelatedPerson, or Organization. That is less unified than CodeableReference, but it meets the source-actor goal without forcing existing `reportOrigin` data through a new JSON shape.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a less optimal old name and two related fields, but avoids invalidating coded R4 origins and still supports actor references.

evidence.detail: R4 reportOrigin is 0..1 CodeableConcept bound to immunization-origin.
R6 informationSource is 0..1 CodeableReference with Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, and Organization targets.

examples.examplesMd: Concept-only R6 informationSource can be mapped back to R4 reportOrigin; reference-valued informationSource cannot be represented in R4 without an extension or loss.

findings.narrativeMd: The secondarily reported source field is renamed and widened. Code that reads or writes `reportOrigin` will miss the R6 field, and code generated from R6 will expose a CodeableReference rather than a CodeableConcept.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: `reportOrigin` is an unknown element and fails strict R6 validation. R6-to-R4: coded concepts can map back, but source actor references cannot be represented by R4 `reportOrigin`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map R4 `reportOrigin` to `informationSource.concept`. For R6 source references, choose a local extension, external Provenance, or manual mapping policy for R4 exports. Regression tests should include both concept and reference forms.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The cleaner R6 name and richer datatype are understandable, but compatibility aliases or an additive reference element would have reduced breakage for systems already using coded origins.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `reportOrigin` is renamed and reshaped into `informationSource` CodeableReference. The R6 goal of naming a concrete information source is reasonable, but invalidating an existing coded-origin field was not necessary to support that goal. Source provenance for secondarily reported immunizations can be important for registry trust and public-health exchange, and a modest additive design appears available.
keyEvidence: R4 `reportOrigin` is 0..1 CodeableConcept bound by example to `immunization-origin`.
R6 `informationSource` is 0..1 CodeableReference bound to the same origin ValueSet and can reference Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, RelatedPerson, or Organization.
The R6 binding name remains `ImmunizationReportOrigin`, supporting the path-level continuity of the coded-origin concept.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3/trial-use makes compatibility for established immunization provenance fields relevant; it is not low-FMM experimental content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `reportOrigin` use a removed property name; R6 source references also create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes: keep `reportOrigin` for coded origin and add an optional source actor/reference field, or at least stage the rename with a deprecated alias. The tradeoff is two related source fields instead of one CodeableReference.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high impact and available less-breaking alternative are supported by the fresh review.

findings.title: recorded was removed from Immunization

oldState.summary: R4 had optional recorded dateTime for when the immunization was first captured in the subject's record.

semanticText.definition: The date the occurrence of the immunization was first captured in the record - potentially significantly after the occurrence of the event.

oldState.narrativeMd: This element distinguished administration occurrence from record-capture timing.

newState.narrativeMd: No same-name replacement appears in the R6 Immunization StructureDefinition. `meta.lastUpdated` is inherited Resource metadata and is not semantically equivalent to first capture in the subject's record.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `recorded` will fail strict R6 validation because the property is no longer in the content model. The migration impact is high when systems rely on record-capture date for provenance, data quality, or registry synchronization, because no local R6 element preserves the exact meaning.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Capture date can affect audit, source reliability, and distinguishing historical recall from administration time.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly remove redundant or provenance-like metadata from Immunization.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `recorded` as optional, possibly deprecated, while recommending Provenance or extensions for richer capture metadata.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local inputs do not show a replacement or rationale for removing a field that can carry distinct capture-time information. If the goal was model cleanup or a shift to Provenance, immediate base removal seems more disruptive than necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep the optional R4 `recorded` element in R6 with clearer text that Provenance is preferred for new implementations. That preserves R4 data while allowing the ecosystem to migrate away from the legacy field over time.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains one legacy provenance-like field but preserves historical capture dates and old instance validity.

evidence.detail: R4 includes recorded 0..1 dateTime.
No R6 snapshot element with id Immunization.recorded is present.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows a historical dose recorded later; R6 has no direct local field for the later capture date.

findings.narrativeMd: `recorded` is a true local removal. Existing R4 data can carry two clinically important times: when vaccination occurred and when it was first captured. R6 keeps occurrence but removes the local capture timestamp.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: old instances with `recorded` are invalid unless the data is dropped or moved. R6-to-R4 is not applicable for this removed element. Generated R6 classes will not have a property for it.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory use of `recorded`. If the value is material, preserve it in a standard extension, Provenance, AuditEvent, or source-system metadata according to local policy. Do not blindly map it to `meta.lastUpdated` unless that timestamp truly has the same meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated optional element or standard extension would have been less disruptive. The removal may be justified by a broader provenance model, but that rationale was not available in the supplied package files.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `recorded` is removed with no direct R6 Immunization replacement. The field distinguishes event occurrence from first capture in the subject's record, which can matter for historical recalls, registry synchronization, audit, and data-quality workflows. Dropping or relocating that timestamp is lossy and policy-dependent.
keyEvidence: R4 `Immunization.recorded` is 0..1 dateTime for when the occurrence was first captured in the record.
No R6 snapshot element with id `Immunization.recorded` is present.
`meta.lastUpdated` is inherited resource metadata and is not the same as first capture in the subject record.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3/trial-use gives meaningful stability pressure for a provenance-like field in a mature public-health resource.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing `recorded` have an unknown local property in R6 and cannot preserve the value without another representation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes: retain `recorded` as optional/deprecated while recommending Provenance or extensions for richer capture metadata. The tradeoff is carrying a legacy timestamp field longer.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly called out old-instance invalidity, lossy migration, and a plausible less-breaking base design.

findings.title: education backbone was removed

oldState.summary: R4 had repeating education BackboneElement with documentType, reference, publicationDate, and presentationDate; imm-1 required documentType or reference.

constraints.human: One of documentType or reference SHALL be present

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could record educational material presented to the patient or guardian at administration time.

newState.summary: R6 has no Immunization.education element or child elements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds broad `supportingInformation` references, but that is not a structural or semantic replacement for inline education metadata.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `education` is invalid against R6. The prevalence is uncertain, but when used it captures patient-facing education/audit data with no direct R6 local replacement.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Vaccine information statement or educational-material tracking can be a legal, public-health, or consent-related requirement in some jurisdictions.

justification.inferredGoal: Possibly move education documentation outside the Immunization resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the optional `education` backbone as deprecated or add a formal replacement path before removing it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The removal may reflect a desire to move education evidence elsewhere, but the supplied definitions do not identify a direct replacement. Given legal and public-health uses for education documentation, immediate removal appears avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained the R4 education backbone for compatibility while documenting preferred use of DocumentReference, Communication, `supportingInformation`, or a standard extension. That would preserve existing records and let profiles narrow or deprecate the old representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps jurisdiction-specific education tracking in the base model, but avoids data loss and old-instance invalidity.

evidence.detail: R4 education is a repeating BackboneElement with child fields and imm-1.
No R6 Immunization.education element or children are present.
R6 supportingInformation is broad Reference(Resource), not a typed inline education replacement.

findings.title: programEligibility changed from CodeableConcept to a backbone with required program and status

oldState.summary: R4 programEligibility was 0..* CodeableConcept bound by example to immunization-program-eligibility.

justification.inferredGoal: Refresh example terminology and move some terminology assets to THO canonicals.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Required status codes appear unchanged; the observed changes are example/extensible terminology and canonical updates, not a base R4-to-R6 validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The clinical rationale for the example ValueSet edits cannot be fully assessed without expansions or official terminology notes. However, the local evidence does not show a required-code removal that would make R4 base instances invalid in R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is not a breaking base-design change, `Yes` or `Partial` alternatives would overcount migration aids as design alternatives. ConceptMaps, release notes, and terminology-server guidance are useful mitigations for tooling and profiles, but they are not backward-compatible base-resource alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Terminology refresh can affect tooling and local profiles, but no less-breaking base design is implicated by unchanged required codes.

evidence.detail: R4 and R6 compose both include completed, entered-in-error, and not-done from event-status.
Local compose changed one SNOMED example code: R4 includes 281657000 while R6 includes 14747002.
R4 local compose includes NASINHLC; R6 local compose does not.
R6 adds ActReason codes and removes the R4 SNOMED is-a filter from local compose.
Several R6 example binding canonicals point to terminology.hl7.org ValueSets not present in the local core package.

examples.examplesMd: Because the affected bindings are example-strength or extensible, these terminology differences are not shown as old-valid/new-invalid base instances. They are still relevant for picklists, generated enums, local profiles, and terminology mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: Terminology changed in several places, but the highest-risk required binding (`status`) did not show code-list changes in the local packages. The practical risk is mainly implementation behavior: code generators, forms, mappings, and local profiles may have assumed the R4 example sets.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base R4-to-R6 validation should not fail solely from these example-binding changes. Runtime systems that validate example bindings as warnings, generate enums from them, or bind UI choices tightly can experience behavior changes. R6-to-R4 representability is low risk for base resources but may be higher under local profiles.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not treat example ValueSets as hard constraints in base migration. Refresh picklists and terminology maps, and review local profiles that strengthen these bindings. Use a terminology server expansion and official ConceptMaps before making clinical code substitutions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The required status binding stability is a good compatibility property. For example sets, backward compatibility depends on tooling conventions; publishing explicit ConceptMaps would reduce ambiguity without constraining the base resource.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No terminology-server expansion was available, and several R6 terminology.hl7.org ValueSets referenced from bindings were not in the local core package.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required `status` codes are unchanged, while the observed terminology movement is in example or extensible bindings and ValueSet metadata/canonicals. Picklists, generated examples, or local profiles may need review, but base R4 Immunization instances should not become invalid solely because an example ValueSet changed.
keyEvidence: R4 and R6 `ValueSet-immunization-status` both include `completed`, `entered-in-error`, and `not-done` from event-status.
R4/R6 `immunization-reason`, `immunization-route`, and `immunization-status-reason` local compose content changed, but these bindings are example strength on the base resource.
Several R6 bindings point to terminology.hl7.org ValueSets for THO-owned terminology, which is canonical/tooling churn rather than an instance-shape break.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 3/trial-use warrants checking required bindings, but example-binding changes do not become hard compatibility problems because of maturity alone.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: example ValueSet content and canonical changes can affect UI lists, generated documentation, or local strengthened profiles, but not base R4-to-R6 instance validity.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable: no required-code removal was found. ConceptMaps and release notes would help implementers, but they are migration aids rather than less-breaking base R6 designs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly noted unchanged required status codes and no base alternative; the fresh review downgrades the finding to No problem for base compatibility.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R6 Immunization is present with the same canonical URL, id, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag. Status changed draft to active but does not change instance shape.

No local top-level minimum-cardinality increase was found for core required elements such as `status`, `vaccineCode`, `patient`, or `occurrence[x]`. Cardinality changes that are material are captured in findings: `protocolApplied.doseNumber` min decreases and `programEligibility` adds required child elements inside a remodeled backbone.

Material local type changes are captured as findings. Other unchanged clinical fields such as `status`, `vaccineCode`, `patient`, `encounter`, `location`, `site`, `route`, `doseQuantity`, `lotNumber`, and `expirationDate` retain their broad type domains.

No R4 reference target removals were found for unchanged local reference elements. Target additions and CodeableReference target effects are captured in findings for `performer.actor`, `manufacturer`, `informationSource`, `reason`, and added R6 elements.

The required `status` binding still contains `completed`, `entered-in-error`, and `not-done` in the local R4/R6 ValueSets. Example/extensible binding changes are captured as a terminology finding; expansion-level clinical equivalence was not established.
Local modifier semantics for `status` and `isSubpotent` remain; no new local Immunization element was found with a new `isModifier=true` flag. Inherited modifierExtension changes are out of scope.

Existing local summary flags did not show a material breaking change. R6 adds `basedOn` as a summary element, which is covered under R6-only optional additions and affects down-version representation, not R4-to-R6 validity.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were identified on Immunization elements.
No local slicing changes were found in the Immunization snapshot elements reviewed.
Material serialization changes are captured in findings for renamed fields, choice-to-non-choice changes, same-path type replacements, and CodeableReference wrapping.

The only local non-inherited constraints found as material are the new R6 root invariants `imm-1` and `imm-2`, plus removal of the old education constraint as part of education removal. Inherited ele-1/dom-* differences are out of scope.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The status metadata changed, but the canonical URL, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag stayed aligned. This does not by itself change instance validation shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tooling that filters by artifact maturity may treat the R6 resource differently.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: vaccineCode comment now explicitly discusses granularity and multiple codings
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The cardinality, datatype, and example binding strength did not materially change. The added explanation clarifies use of multiple codings such as NDC and CVX within a CodeableConcept.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers should preserve multiple codings during migration rather than collapsing product-level and class-level codes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: occurrence guidance expanded around date/time, time zones, partial dates, and self-administered series
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element remains mandatory 1..1 with dateTime|string choices. The change is semantic guidance rather than a structural validator change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Migration and analytics should avoid shifting immunization dates across time zones and should preserve string dates when exact dates are unknown.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: statusReason text mentions entered-in-error even though a new invariant only allows not-done
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The text change alone is not the breaking mechanism; the associated invariant is reported separately as a hard constraint finding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Reviewers should reconcile the text/invariant mismatch before enforcing local migration rules for `entered-in-error` reasons.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Many local Immunization changes depend on the R6-only CodeableReference datatype. The datatype's own cross-version representation and serializer behavior should be assessed in its assigned report.
Snapshot differences in inherited children, inherited constraints, and base comments were deliberately excluded under the scope rule and should be owned by base-artifact reports.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: Immunization-related ValueSets, including terminology.hl7.org immunization-function, immunization-funding-source, immunization-program-eligibility, and immunization-subpotent-reason
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 bindings reference THO ValueSet canonicals not present as local core package files, and no terminology expansions were performed. Terminology-specific review should verify code continuity and ConceptMaps.

Element renames/removals such as `reason`, `informationSource`, `recorded`, and protocol dose fields may affect search parameters or server query behavior, which was outside this StructureDefinition-focused report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, migration guide, work-group notes, or Jira rationale was available locally. Backward-compatibility and justification assessments are inferred from computable definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official HL7 R6 ballot change notes, Jira tickets, and published cross-version diff for Immunization.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local ValueSet compose content and local CodeSystem files only. SNOMED CT expansions and external terminology.hl7.org ValueSets were not expanded.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run R4 and R6 expansions using a terminology server with the appropriate SNOMED and THO versions, then compare removed, added, and meaning-changed codes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Illustrative examples were reasoned from StructureDefinitions but not run through an R4/R6 validator in this session.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Validate representative R4 and transformed R6 Immunization instances with official validators and conversion tooling.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Implementation guides and profiles may strengthen bindings, add must-support expectations, or define migration extensions. This report covers the base core resource only.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review jurisdictional immunization profiles, registry guides, and local conformance rules after the base-resource assessment.
